title: Pneumonia, lung abscess, empyema and respiratory arrest in the hospital
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the main lung condition (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/18/2026
Reason for Admission: Shortness of breath, productive cough, and fever.

Vitals:
BP: 118/74
HR: 82 (RRR)
RR: 18
Temp: 99.1 F
SpO2: 95% on RA

Recent Labs:
WBC: 14.5 (Elevated)
Hgb: 11.2
Hct: 33.8
Cr: 1.1
eGFR: 62
Lactic Acid: 1.2

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Positive for fever, malaise.
Respiratory: Positive for cough, dyspnea. Denies wheezing.
CV: Denies chest pain.
GI: Denies nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea.
MSK: Denies joint pain.

Social History:
Retired. Lives in assisted living facility. Non-smoker.

Family History:
Mother: Hypertension.
Father: Type 2 Diabetes.

Hospital Course:
Pt is an 85-year-old female admitted with worsening respiratory symptoms. CXR and bedside ultrasound confirmed a large empyema in the right pleural space. Pt underwent bedside placement of a chest tube for drainage of the empyema. Drainage was purulent. Pt was started on IV antibiotics. Progress was made over 6 days; drainage volume decreased and inflammatory markers improved. Chest tube was removed on 05/17/2026 as drainage was minimal and pt remained afebrile. Pt is stable for discharge to assisted living.

Discharge Diagnoses:
Right-sided empyema.

Discharge Medications:
Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125mg BID (Finish 7-day course).
Acetaminophen 650mg PRN for pain/fever.

Follow-up:
F/u with PCP in 1 week for wound check and reassessment of respiratory status.

Electronically signed,
D. Kowalski, MD
05/18/2026
refs: ICD-10-CM Tabular: J15-J18, J69, J85-J86, R09

distractors.why: Pus in the pleural space is empyema, not a plain effusion.
